- If sentiment is negative or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is consistently positive, model often overshoots upward; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak or mean of last 5 days.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overcorrects downward; delay downward adjustment by 1–2 periods unless sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce forecast by 1–3% per period until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to drift toward historical mean; anchor forecast to 30-day moving average unless sentiment shifts.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often underestimates upward momentum; add 1–2% buffer if sentiment is positive and price is trending up.
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model overestimates upside; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 2 periods.
